subject.title: [codex] Keep full-auto Codex exec from stale relay decline

question: Is rerunning the direct OpenClaw before-tool-call hook an authoritative replacement for an unavailable native relay when Codex is in full-auto mode?
rationale: The patch intentionally relaxes a fail-closed approval path, and source-level plausibility alone cannot establish that no native-only policy is lost when the relay transport disappears.

options.title: Approve the narrow exception after proof
options.body: Confirm hook-policy equivalence and require a live unavailable-relay success plus explicit-denial failure before merging.

options.title: Retain fail-closed relay handling
options.body: Keep relay unavailability blocking until the relay lifecycle is repaired so the existing approval boundary remains unchanged.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow exception after proof
recommendation.body: Confirm hook-policy equivalence and require a live unavailable-relay success plus explicit-denial failure before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced much of the native relay infrastructure and is best positioned to confirm whether direct-hook evaluation preserves the intended policy boundary.
